key_insight: GRASP turns probabilistic logic program learning into gradient boosting, using an LLM to propose candidate first-order rules while preserving interpretable weighted rule ensembles.
engineering_relevance: This gives practitioners a practical way to learn transparent neurosymbolic models for relational data without relying on brute-force symbolic search.
method: Treats each weak learner as a first-order logic rule in a boosting framework.
Uses functional gradients to guide which rules should be added next.
Delegates hard inner-loop search to an LLM proposal oracle for hypothesis generation.
evidence_signal: The method is evaluated on four relational benchmarks, including Tox21, mutagenesis, and Cora, and is reported to outperform symbolic, neural, and LLM-only baselines.
watch_item: Performance and reliability may depend on the quality of LLM-proposed rules, so search bias or invalid hypotheses remain a practical concern.
paper_title: Learning Probabilistic Logic Programs with Functional Gradient Guided Language Models
